title: On the margins of history
summary: Popular classes, memory and political autonomy.
body:
Course themes

  • Subalternity, popular culture and representation
  • Archives and the recovery of popular voices
  • Moral economy, subsistence and the right to existence
  • Housing and organisation
  • Militant memory, working-class literature and history from below

What will we work on?

Producing a short piece of work that examines who leaves a trace in the sources and how to recover the voices left out of the story.

Context and approach

Historical narratives have given pride of place to rulers, battles and great figures. This course asks how the popular classes interpret their living conditions and build forms of autonomous organisation. Debates on popular culture and subalternity will also allow us to discuss the limits of archives and of the institutions that have preserved these voices.

E. P. Thompson’s moral economy of the crowd, the right to existence and the work of Peter Linebaugh and Marcus Rediker will open connections with present-day conflicts. Readings will be combined with a short piece of work on a historical or current conflict, drawing on sources, the workers’ press or oral memory.
introduction: What do we know about the people who changed history from below? An exploration of the ways of life, ideas and struggles of the popular classes, and of the problems involved in recovering their voices.
